cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: The Plan Gets Better
cards.instruction: Celebrate every setback as proof that the scheme is becoming more sophisticated, selective, or impossible to detect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only six people solved our supper-club invitation. Excellent. A more selective guest list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Five wanted a puzzle night. They've cancelled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then remove them from 'dinner guests'. We are refining the audience, not counting absences.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The last one's the printer. Shall I just pay him at the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better: a supplier dinner. Seat him before you settle anything. Please don't conduct our new partnership on the doorstep.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 celebrates a small solved-invitation count; A3 corrects B2's cancellations into audience refinement; A5 corrects B4's doorstep-payment plan into supplier hospitality, celebrating a newly exclusive event.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 wrong-expectation cancellations cause A3 reclassification. B4 printer-only payment visit supplies both the perceived setback and the specific action A5 changes.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants realistic attendance and B4 proposes a practical way to settle the remaining visitor. A's optimistic hosting responds to this useful organizing role.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 creditor encounter into a more selective business dinner and makes B act on the improved-plan claim.

specificity.evidence: A1 supper-club invitation puzzle, B2 mistaken puzzle-night guests and B4 printer needing payment establish the event's collapse.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's seat-before-payment direction and doorstep rebuke serve hospitality rather than a standalone joke about failure.

coach2.stated: A1 six solved invitations; B2 five cancel; B4 remaining printer wants payment and B proposes paying at door.
coach2.inferred: A wants to see the event as increasingly useful, while B is handling attendance and logistics.
coach2.missing: No prior supplier partnership exists as fact; A is proposing the new interpretation and behavior.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate; the new sophistication is caused by B4's actual visitor rather than an invented late benefactor.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 explains why A1's six guests have mostly cancelled.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 treats B2 cancellations as helpful filtering and corrects the list category.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 identifies the final visitor's payment purpose and offers a practical response.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 changes B4 doorstep settlement into seated hospitality and celebrates a new supplier partnership.

reservation: Calling a creditor a partnership guest may not persuade him. The character's confident reframing is the game, not a prediction of success.
